bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to cannabis; modifying use of proceeds from the cannabis gross receipts tax; establishing the cannabis youth grant program; requiring a report; amending Minnesota Statutes 2025 Supplement, section 295.81, subdivision 10; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 342.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2025 Supplement, section 295.81, subdivision 10, is amended to read:

Subd. 10.
Deposit of revenues; account established.
[+(a) +]The commissioner must deposit the revenues, including penalties and interest, derived from the tax imposed by this section in the general fund.

[+(b) Of the amount deposited under paragraph (a), ten percent is annually appropriated to the commissioner of children, youth, and families for the cannabis youth grant program under section 342.71. +]

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective for gross receipts received after June 30, 2026. +]

Sec. 2.

[+[342.71] CANNABIS YOUTH GRANT PROGRAM. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Establishment.+]

[+The office must establish a cannabis youth grant program to award grants to programs that promote positive youth development, young people's self-sufficient transition into adulthood, and young people's health. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Eligible programs.+]

[+(a) Cannabis youth grants must be awarded to programs that do at least one of the following: +]

[+(1) provide high quality after-school, summer, or youth employment, training, and entrepreneurship opportunities as a primary prevention and skill-building strategy; +]

[+(2) employ peer-led youth education and mentorship programs that equip young people with accurate information, leadership skills, and decision-making tools that mitigate cannabis use; or +]

[+(3) invest in youth-led restorative justice initiatives that address past harms of cannabis criminalization and promote positive community engagement. +]

[+(b) Cannabis youth grants must be awarded to programs with the following goals: +]

[+(1) building young people's financial management, employment, and entrepreneurship skills; +]

[+(2) improving mental health and young people's sense of belonging in community; +]

[+(3) preventing early use of cannabis and other controlled substances; and +]

[+(4) building young people's community engagement and leadership skills. +]

[+(c) The cannabis youth grant program must prioritize communities disproportionately impacted by cannabis-related criminalization while ensuring statewide distribution. +]

[+Subd. 3.+]

[+Applications.+]

[+Eligible programs must apply for cannabis youth grants on forms prescribed by the office, describing how the program meets the eligibility requirements in subdivision 2. +]

[+Subd. 4.+]

[+Reporting requirements.+]

[+The office must submit a report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over cannabis that details the cannabis youth grants awarded, including the amount of money awarded, the use of grant money, and the programs awarded grants. +]

[+EFFECTIVE DATE.+]

[+This section is effective July 1, 2026. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to cannabis; modifying use of proceeds from the cannabis gross receipts tax; establishing the cannabis youth grant program; requiring a report; amending Minnesota Statutes 2025 Supplement, section 295.81, subdivision 10; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 342.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2025 Supplement, section 295.81, subdivision 10, is amended to read:

Subd. 10.
Deposit of revenues; account established.
(a) The commissioner must deposit the revenues, including penalties and interest, derived from the tax imposed by this section in the general fund.

(b) Of the amount deposited under paragraph (a), ten percent is annually appropriated to the commissioner of children, youth, and families for the cannabis youth grant program under section 342.71.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective for gross receipts received after June 30, 2026.

Sec. 2.

[342.71] CANNABIS YOUTH GRANT PROGRAM.

Subdivision 1.

Establishment.

The office must establish a cannabis youth grant program to award grants to programs that promote positive youth development, young people's self-sufficient transition into adulthood, and young people's health.

Subd. 2.

Eligible programs.

(a) Cannabis youth grants must be awarded to programs that do at least one of the following:

(1) provide high quality after-school, summer, or youth employment, training, and entrepreneurship opportunities as a primary prevention and skill-building strategy;

(2) employ peer-led youth education and mentorship programs that equip young people with accurate information, leadership skills, and decision-making tools that mitigate cannabis use; or

(3) invest in youth-led restorative justice initiatives that address past harms of cannabis criminalization and promote positive community engagement.

(b) Cannabis youth grants must be awarded to programs with the following goals:

(1) building young people's financial management, employment, and entrepreneurship skills;

(2) improving mental health and young people's sense of belonging in community;

(3) preventing early use of cannabis and other controlled substances; and

(4) building young people's community engagement and leadership skills.

(c) The cannabis youth grant program must prioritize communities disproportionately impacted by cannabis-related criminalization while ensuring statewide distribution.

Subd. 3.

Applications.

Eligible programs must apply for cannabis youth grants on forms prescribed by the office, describing how the program meets the eligibility requirements in subdivision 2.

Subd. 4.

Reporting requirements.

The office must submit a report to the chairs and ranking minority members of the legislative committees with jurisdiction over cannabis that details the cannabis youth grants awarded, including the amount of money awarded, the use of grant money, and the programs awarded grants.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective July 1, 2026.
